mil3.3.9:0.3: 9. The Question on the Mark of Feeling
mil3.3.9:1.1: “Sir Nagasena, what is the mark of feeling”?
mil3.3.9:1.2: “Feeling is marked by being felt, Great King, and by being experienced”.
mil3.3.9:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, that a certain man did a service for the king, and the king was pleased with him and granted him a reward. He would serve the king with that reward, endowed with and possessing the five sense pleasures. Then he would think: ‘in the past I did a service for the king, and the king, pleased, granted me a reward, so now, caused by that, I experience a feeling of just this sort’.
mil3.3.9:3.1: Or else, Great King, suppose a certain man did a wholesome deed and, at the breaking up of his body, at his final death, was reborn in a good destination, in the world of heaven. There too he would serve, endowed with and possessing the five sense pleasures bestowed from above. Then he would think: ‘in the past I did a wholesome deed, so now, caused by that, I experience a feeling of just this sort’.
mil3.3.9:3.2: Thus, Great King, feeling is marked by being felt, and by being experienced”.
mil3.3.9:5.1: The Question on the Mark of Feeling, ninth.
